## Defect

`rebar-observability.service` was not publishing sparsely; it was being killed part-way through many runs under I/O load. The unit has `TimeoutStartSec=240s`; journal evidence from 2026-09-05 showed runs spanning exactly four minutes and exiting `code=killed, status=15/TERM`, with only ~34-40s CPU. Metrics after the kill point vanished, making truncation indistinguishable from healthy silence under `treat_missing_data = breaching`.

Root cause: independently reasonable per-section bounds composed into an impossible whole-run budget. The old shape allowed two Docker `du` walks alone to consume 240s, before later Docker ledger, journal, var/tmp, container, memory, marker, and mirror sections ran.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Cumulative attribution by measurement: per-section elapsed time was summed against the 240s budget, naming the consuming sections and accounting for existing per-call bounds.
- [x] The reserve is enforced by an absolute deadline, not by reservation: the probe records `PROBE_STARTED_AT`; `probe_budget_left` computes `PROBE_DEADLINE_SEC - elapsed - PROBE_TAIL_RESERVE_SEC`; every wall-clock-bounded call receives `min(own ceiling, budget_left)` floored at 1s.
- [x] Verified by asserting the GRANT each call receives: exhausted budget gives the 1s floor; full budget gives the call's own ceiling.
- [x] Every bounded call routes through the one `clamped` helper; the source-scan guard fails if a call site bypasses it.
- [x] The clamped portion is bounded by construction at `PROBE_DEADLINE_SEC - PROBE_TAIL_RESERVE_SEC` = 160s, leaving an 80s tail margin under the 240s unit timeout.
- [x] `PROBE_DEADLINE_SEC` equals the unit's `TimeoutStartSec`, enforced by tests against `install-observability.sh`.
- [x] The probe completes within timeout under representative load over consecutive runs.
- [x] A truncated run cannot be silent: `ExecStopPost --report-exit` publishes/logs `probe_truncated`; normal completion publishes `probe_ok` and `probe_elapsed_seconds` at the end.
- [x] The truncation signal needs no network call in the normal path: the report hook reads cached region first and logs to journald even if metric publication cannot happen.
- [x] Defect-seeded: tests drive calls past the whole budget; late metrics still get their turn and the completion signal fires.
- [x] Alarm surface remeasured: false gap/truncation shape cleared without threshold changes; remaining BuildKit alarm is a real >85% value, not missing-data truncation.
- [x] Back-out path: normal Gerrit/autodeploy rollback of landed probe commits.
- [x] Portability: host shell + systemd + local validation; no single-CI-provider dependence.

## Close evidence (2026-09-07)

- Landed implementation: `aaa31f11f3bc` / `84ef284833be` (comments record Gerrit gate success and follow-up alarm-window fix).
- Targeted validation on current `origin/main` worktree: `python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_timeout_9313.py tests/scripts/test_observability_memory_9ea3.py tests/unit/test_gate_peak_rss_9ea3.py -q` -> 50 passed in 137.42s.
- CloudWatch window 2026-09-07T00:29:49Z..03:29:49Z: `probe_ok` 31 datapoints, all max=1; `probe_truncated` 31 datapoints, all max=0; `probe_elapsed_seconds` max=128s (<240s).
- Former tail metrics are publishing current datapoints in the same window: Docker storage/buildkit/unaccounted/container gauges each had 25 datapoints with last samples at 20:24 PDT; journal, var/tmp, memory, and container census gauges each had 33 datapoints.
- Alarm surface: `rebar-container-writable-usage-high` and `rebar-var-tmp-usage-high` are OK. `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` remains ALARM because the latest datapoint is 104% > 85%; that is a true capacity breach, not the former silent truncation/position-dependent gap.

## Provenance

Found 2026-09-05 while investigating missing `mem_used_percent`. The journal evidence proved truncation; CloudWatch before/after proved the landed budget composition fixed the dead-publisher shape.
